items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: There’s Hasidic pop recordings too, in Brooklyn. Mordechai Ben David, Avraham Fried, all those guys, Yeedle, all of them.

ctx.x: Well you make plans in your life based on what’s going on around you at the time. But everything changes and you have to be willing to change with the style of music. I know when I first got to New York, 1970, the studio recording scene was in a transition from big band and jazz to rock & roll. And there were a lot of guys like bass players, drummers — oh this rock & roll thing’s never going to catch on, I don’t want to play that junk. You know they used a different word. And so, and those guys were out of the…

to be the same twelve notes. But you have to be able to play jazz, you have to play Latin, you have to play classical, you have to play whatever style of music, you just have to play it. There’s Hasidic pop recordings too, in Brooklyn. Mordechai Ben David, Avraham Fried, all those guys, Yeedle, all of them. They dress up like the Blues Brothers too.

Yes I noticed that. I just read, I thought it was pretty hip that, the way that thing came together and Dan Akroyd, your first assignment, if this is true, said, “Write an arrangement for some horn parts for Rocket 88.”
